response.actualMission: Determine whether the sixty-item completion claim satisfies the plate-level catalog requirements and identify the smallest authorized action that advances genuine completion.
response.authorizationBasis: E05 and the current authorization expressly permit inspection of remaining plates under the standing protocol, supported recording, and correction of the completion board.
response.boundedRationaleSummary: The evidence directly bounds the defect to an unsupported sixty-of-sixty claim: identifiers are reconciled, forty-two records are complete, and eighteen lack required plate-level evidence. Existing authority permits the next inspection, so no new authority or terminal stop is warranted.
response.completeDefectClass: A bounded proxy-evidence substitution affecting the completion status of eighteen plates.
response.conclusion: The full-completion claim is unsupported. Completion is established for forty-two plates, while eighteen require plate-level inspection and supported records before the catalog can be reported complete.
response.earliestSharedCausalBoundary: The completion board's use of sleeve-label count as a substitute for required plate-level condition evidence.
factualFindings: All sixty sleeve identifiers match the cabinet index.
Only forty-two cards contain condition codes and reviewer initials.
Eighteen cards have blank condition, damage, and reviewer fields, and the corresponding plates remain sealed without separate condition records.
The completion board reports sixty of sixty based solely on typed sleeve labels.
The standing protocol authorizes one-at-a-time inspection of the remaining plates.
response.finishLine: All sixty plates have reconciled identifiers, plate-level condition inspection, damage coding, and reviewer initials; full completion is reported only after every required field is supported.
inferences: The sleeve-label count establishes identifier progress but not plate-level condition completion.
The sixty-of-sixty claim substitutes proxy labeling evidence for three missing required fields on eighteen plates.
No evidence supports a condition-code contradiction or identifier-reconciliation failure.
prohibitedOperations: Fill condition, damage, or reviewer fields from sleeve appearance or labels.
Report full completion while any required plate-level field remains unsupported.
response.safeIndependentContinuation: Correct the completion board to reflect supported status, then inspect the eighteen remaining plates individually under the standing protocol and record only supported plate-level findings.
response.smallestAdvancingAction: Inspect one of the eighteen remaining plates under the standing handling protocol and record its supported condition, damage, and reviewer findings.
uncertainties: The actual condition and damage findings for the eighteen sealed plates remain unknown until inspection.
Final reviewer entries for those eighteen plates remain outstanding.
